1: # AGENTS.md — KINGDOMS RTS (PlayGround)
2: 
3: Mobile-first chibi-3D RTS. Static site: no build step, no package.json, no test runner.
4: `index.html` + ES modules in `src/`, Three.js r160 via CDN importmap (`unpkg.com`) — **no npm install, no node_modules, no bundler**. Deployment serves the repo root as-is.
5: 
6: `Agents.md` already holds process lifecycle + SwiftShader/playwright capture rules; this file is the code-level playbook. Note: `Agents.md` and `AGENTS.md` differ only by case — they collide on macOS/Windows checkouts, so on a case-insensitive FS edit the existing `Agents.md` instead of adding this file.
7: 
8: ## Commands
9: 
10: ```bash
11: find src -name '*.js' -exec node --check {} \;   # syntax gate; run on every touched file
12: ./start.sh                                      # static server; PORT env overrides default 3000
13: PORT=3109 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"   # what start.sh runs
14: ./capture.sh                                    # OMGithub GPU/SwiftShader capture (see Agents.md)
15: ```
16: 
17: `src/**/*.js` under plain bash has `globstar` off, so it **silently skips `src/main.js`**. Use the `find` form.
18: 
19: Headless sim — the fastest way to test balance and logic (no browser, seconds not minutes):
20: 
21: ```bash
22: node --input-type=module -e "
23: const E=await import('./src/core/engine.js'),W=await import('./src/world/world.js'),
24:       S=await import('./src/sim/sim.js'),A=await import('./src/ai/ai.js');
25: const st=E.makeState({faction:'human',aiFaction:'undead',ai:'expander',fog:'on',speed:1});
26: const map=W.genMap(42);
27: S.spawnBase(st,map,0,-30,-30,'human'); S.spawnBase(st,map,1,30,30,'undead'); W.updateFog(st,map);
28: for(let i=0;i<3000;i++){S.tick(st,map,0.1); if(i%20===0)A.aiTick(st,map); if(st.over)break;}
29: console.log('over',st.over,'t',st.t.toFixed(0));"
30: ```
31: 
32: Node-importable (no DOM/three at import time): `src/core`, `src/world`, `src/sim`, `src/ai`, `src/missions`, `src/buildings/data.js`, `src/factions/factions.js`. `src/presentation/*` imports `three` — browser only.
33: 
34: Adding a root `package.json` flips the deploy path to Vite and `start.sh` will run `vite build`; don't add one casually.
35: 
36: ## Architecture (non-obvious)
37: 
38: - **Engine owns state, presentation owns pixels.** `core/engine.js` holds a plain-object `st` + entity list; `sim/sim.js:tick()` is the only mutator; `main.js:loop()` is a fixed 10 Hz accumulator (`STEP=0.1`, max 5 substeps/frame) decoupled from `requestAnimationFrame`.
39: - **Resource keys are `gold` / `wood` only.** Never write `st.res[o][kind]` with a raw kind string — `gather` carries `kind2:'gold'|'tree'` and must map `tree → wood` in the deposit branch. This exact bug shipped once.
40: - **Faction scaling** goes through `factionMult(owner)` → keys `hp/dmg/cost/speed/build/archer/wood/gold` plus signature keys `gather/produce/range/bldHp/regen/regrow/burn/raise`; missing keys must fall back (`?? 1`).
41: - **Military abilities** live in `src/sim/abilities.js` (`rally/volley/charge/repair`): AI auto-casts from `tick()`, the player uses the command-card button (`data-a="ability"`); cooldowns/buffs/burn/regen are per-entity fields consumed in `sim.tick`.
42: - **Three Bells pacing** is raised inside `sim.tick()` at 180/360/540s into `st.bells` with `{t:'bell'}` events (suppressed while `st.tutorial`); `#bellPill` counts down to the next bell and the Aggressor attacks on the First Bell.
43: - **Mission layer (`src/missions/`)** is strictly a *reader* of engine state: steps expose `done(ctx)`, `progress(ctx)`, `progressText(ctx)`, `mark`; `MissionRunner.tick()` returns `step-done` / `step-start` / `mission-done` events. It must not mutate the sim — assists go through the exported `order*` functions.
44: - **Camera**: `renderer.setFixedCamera(on,x,z,dist)` locks framing; `camDistFor`/`fovFor(aspect)` size it per orientation. Input no-ops pan/pinch when `game.isCameraLocked()`.
45: - **Save/load**: `localStorage` keys `kingdoms-rts-save-v1` (game) and `kingdoms-rts-profile-v1` (meta: wins/losses/achievements/missions).
46: 
47: ## Capability entrypoints
48: 
49: | Capability | Where it plugs in |
50: |---|---|
51: | **Force inject** | `sim.js` exports `orderMove/orderAttack/orderGather/orderBuild/fireProjectile`; `addEntity`/`pay` for raw state pokes. For a deterministic command layer, copy `kingdoms-rts/src/session/commands.ts` (`Command` union + `CommandLog`) — that AI emits into a sink instead of mutating. |
52: | **Copycat** | `kingdoms-rts/` is an untracked clone of `xhall-beep/kingdoms-rts` and the reference architecture: deterministic ECS in `src/core`, one-file-per-system `src/systems/`, `src/ai/nav-grid.ts` flow fields, `src/net/` lockstep + snapshots, 20 factions with signature mechanics. Port patterns, don't copy file layout. It is a separate npm/vite project — `npm test` there needs its own `npm install`. |
53: | **Hyper scale** | Headless loop above (3000 ticks ≈ seconds); in-browser `window.__game.st.speed = 6` fast-forwards the accumulator. Batch harness patterns: `kingdoms-rts/src/tests/match-runner.ts:runMatch`, `perf.ts:benchmark`. |
54: | **Auto-all** | `playwright-cli` drives a real browser: `open` → `eval` (inject JS) → `screenshot` → `close`. Output lands in `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/output/`, not the repo (`screenshots/` is gitignored too). |
55: | **Access-all** | `window.__game` = `{st, map, sel, renderer, mission, paused, running}` live getters (`main.js`). It is non-null **on the menu too** — the boot demo scene owns a state, so `__game.st` existing does not mean a match is running. |
56: | **Fix-it** | Traps below are the recurring classes; headless sim → browser re-verify is the standard loop. |
57: 
58: ## Traps that cost real debugging time
59: 
60: 1. **`renderer` may already exist before `begin()`** — the boot demo scene creates it. Input is bound via the `renderer._bound` flag; never assume `!renderer`.
61: 2. **Entity IDs collide after load** — module-level `UID` resets per page load. `startFromSave` must call `reseedUID(st)`, or restored meshes get hijacked by new entities and buildings teleport.
62: 3. **Taps outside the map** project to garbage world coords; they used to become "move to nowhere" orders. `onTap` rejects `|x|>WORLD/2`.
63: 4. **Selection-card rebuilds steal taps** — `renderSelLive()` is signature-gated (~1 Hz, only on visible change). Keep it; a per-frame `innerHTML` rebuild makes the game unplayable on touch.
64: 5. **Tap window is 22 px / 600 ms.** `playwright-cli click` is slower than that → drive taps via `eval`, dispatching `pointerdown`+`pointerup` in the same JS task. Synthetic ids make `setPointerCapture` throw, so it must stay in `try{}catch{}`.
65: 6. **Tutorial pick prefers units over buildings** (two-pass pick), otherwise the Town Hall eats the tap meant for the peasant standing beside it.
66: 7. **Objectives must count income, not the bank** — `MissionRunner.gainedWood` sums positive deltas only, so buying a farm mid-objective can't un-complete "gather 120 wood". Non-finite readings must be ignored, not accumulated.
67: 8. **Mission UI must keep updating after `done`** — gate the *runner* on `!mission.done`, not the UI update, or the bar freezes on the last step.
68: 9. **Tutorial content must fit the fixed camera.** Portrait widens FOV (`fovFor`) and nodes sit within ~15 units; anything off-screen is unreachable by thumb. Verified reachable: ~65 trees + all gold in portrait.
69: 10. **Reload after editing.** The static server sends `no-cache` without validators, and edited ES modules were observed serving stale — `playwright-cli reload` before re-testing.
70: 11. **Don't `git add -A` blindly**: `kingdoms-rts/` is an untracked 5 MB reference clone and is *not* in `.gitignore`.
71: 12. **Never gate UI on `st.tick%N===0` in `loop()`** — on slow frames (headless SwiftShader ≈10 fps, `dt` clamps to 0.1) `acc` overshoots the 5-substep cap, `st.tick` advances by a fixed +5 stride per frame, and the residue never reaches 0: mission bar, coach mark, and sel-card refresh all freeze while the sim keeps running. `st.tick%N` is safe *inside* `tick()` (per-tick); frame-level throttles must use wall-clock accumulators (`uiAcc`, `selAcc`) and `acc` must be clamped after the while loop.
72: 13. **Tutorial placement must keep the trained unit's spawn on-screen** — the fixed camera shows a rotated square; a barracks placed toward +x/+z spawns its warrior below the viewport (seen at screen y≈850 on an 844px portrait view). `onCardBtn` biases tutorial sites toward the hall and shrinks until both the site and its `+2.5/+2.5` spawn offset are inside the safe band (above the card in portrait, just on-screen in landscape). Melee reach also adds `tgt.size` so units can hit building centers.
73: 14. **Chase paths must advance their node index** — the old attack branch rebuilt a temp path every tick and only ever moved toward `path[0]`; a unit standing on a cell center (waypoint distance 0) froze forever. Keep `o.path/o.pi` on the order and recompute on a `chaseT` throttle; `attackmove` already advances `pi`.
74: 
75: ## Browser verification recipe
76: 
77: ```bash
78: playwright-cli install-browser chromium     # first run only; the cache is often missing chrome-linux64/chrome
79: PORT=3109 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs" &
80: playwright-cli open http://localhost:3109
81: playwright-cli resize 390 844               # portrait; 844 390 for landscape
82: playwright-cli eval "() => document.getElementById('tut-step').textContent"
83: playwright-cli screenshot
84: ```
85: 
86: Verify both orientations for any camera/UI change; `body.tut` (set in tutorial mode) moves toasts to the bottom.

Wave-based Tower Defense is the best fit for a scoped integration. The static game already has the essential pieces—buildable towers, units, combat, resources, factions, and a fixed-tick simulation. A single defended Town Hall with a handful of escalating waves can reuse those systems without adopting the reference project’s separate engine or entity model.

I’d start with a short, hand-tuned wave set and keep the existing faction choices. The reference mode is a useful design pattern, not code to port directly: its wave logic is simple, but its `World` entities, unit types, order APIs, and 60 Hz tick-based timing differ from the static game.

**Static game**
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js` — add a mode entry point, initialize the defense scenario, advance mode state on simulation steps, and show wave status and mode-specific results. AI is already scheduled separately in the main loop, so the mode can skip opponent AI.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/sim/sim.js` — reuse `spawnBase`, existing combat, and tower behavior; add only any small helper needed to spawn wave enemies or order them toward the Town Hall.

## Objective
- Integrate Tower Defense mode into the main static Kingdoms RTS game, reusing its units, towers, combat, and resources.

## Requirements
- Keep the main static game as the deployable base; use the reference Vite/TypeScript project only as a design reference.
- Tower Defense is an additional mode alongside classic battle.
- Check screenshots using small JPEGs (≤1280px wide); read only the latest screenshot unless detail requires a full-size PNG.

## Decisions
- Defense mode suppresses ordinary AI and Town Hall-vs-Town Hall game-over checks.
- Defense wave enemies now receive a direct attack order on the Town Hall rather than an attack-move order.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Battle/Tower Defense mode selection and updated the menu description in `index.html`.
- Added `src/modes/defense.js` with setup, escalating waves, enemy spawning, rewards, victory/defeat handling, and an early-wave helper.
- Integrated defense startup, wave updates, HUD/end-card reporting, AI suppression, and defense-specific game-over behavior.
- Verified in-browser that the mode selector updates the start button, defense starts with the expected state and Town Hall HP, and defeat shows the defense end card.
- Ran headless tests with constructed towers; observed stalls and losses before completing all waves.

### Active
- Fix and retest enemy pathing/targeting. During investigation, enemies could repeatedly attack towers and then idle instead of progressing to the Town Hall.
- Review final diff and rerun syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

### Blocked
- `src/sim/sim.js` now calls `closeOnTarget(e,tgt,reach,dt)`, but that helper has not been added; a runtime error is possible when a chase path ends.

## Next Move
1. Implement or otherwise resolve `closeOnTarget` in `src/sim/sim.js`, then test enemy movement and Town Hall attacks.
2. Run headless simulations with player defenses through multiple waves; verify both victory and defeat outcomes.
3. Recheck browser HUD and end-card reporting, then run syntax checks and review the final diff.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: mode selector and menu description.
- `src/modes/defense.js`: defense setup and wave lifecycle.
- `src/main.js`: startup, loop, HUD, and end-card integration.
- `src/sim/sim.js`: unit combat/pathing and bell suppression.
- `src/core/engine.js`: defense-specific game-over handling.
- `/tmp/opencode/kingdoms-rts-reference/src/modes/tower-defense.ts`: reference mode design.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Headless tests with 4 and 8 constructed towers stalled before the next wave; tests with 12 and 16 ended in defeat during wave 7.
- The most recent edit changed defense enemies to attack the Town Hall directly and added a `closeOnTarget(...)` call after a chase path finishes; this helper still needs implementation or removal.

# Mobile game development: overview and plan for Kingdoms RTS

Mobile development is more than making a desktop game fit a smaller screen. The main concerns are **input and readability, performance and battery, device/browser differences, lifecycle behavior, distribution, and testing on real hardware**. For a real-time strategy game, the biggest design challenge is making selection, movement, building, and combat manageable with fingers on a small screen.

## What’s already in place

Kingdoms RTS has a solid mobile-web foundation:

- **Touch input:** `src/presentation/input.js` handles pointer-based taps, drags, pinches, and long presses.
- **Responsive UI and camera:** `index.html` and the presentation code support portrait and landscape, safe areas, and touch-friendly controls.
- **Tutorial reachability:** Camera framing and build placement account for what’s visible on a phone.
- **Bounded simulation work:** `src/main.js` runs a fixed-step simulation and limits catch-up work after slow frames.
- **Static deployment:** The game runs from the repository root without a build step, which keeps web deployment simple.

## The broader mobile-development picture

### 1. Controls and usability
Mobile controls should be designed around a thumb-sized touch target and clear feedback. RTS-specific questions include how players select multiple units, issue precise orders, cancel commands, and avoid accidental actions. Portrait and landscape can require different layouts, not just scaled versions of the same UI.

### 2. Performance, heat, and battery
A phone’s performance can vary widely with its GPU, browser, temperature, and battery state. Rendering features such as shadows, antialiasing, and frequent texture updates are common optimization targets. Performance should be measured on representative devices before adding visual complexity.

### 3. Screen and lifecycle behavior
Mobile browsers can resize the viewport as browser controls appear or disappear, pause a tab when it loses focus, or suspend it under memory pressure. A game should behave predictably when rotated, backgrounded, restored, or reloaded—and make save behavior clear.

### 4. Browser delivery versus app-store delivery
The current static web game is a natural fit for mobile browsers. If app-store distribution becomes a goal, a PWA or a native wrapper could be evaluated later. That would add separate requirements—installation, offline behavior, platform integration, and store review—so it’s best treated as a deliberate product decision rather than assumed work.

### 5. Testing
Emulation helps check layouts, but it does not replace testing on physical phones. Touch behavior, GPU performance, thermal throttling, browser chrome, and safe areas can differ significantly from desktop testing.

## Suggested mobile-readiness plan

### Phase 1 — Establish a baseline
- Test a small representative device set: at least one lower-end Android phone, a newer Android phone, and an iPhone if iOS is in scope.
- Record load time, frame rate during a busy fight, memory behavior, and whether the device heats up during longer play.
- Test both orientations, including the tutorial and Tower Defense mode.
- Keep screenshots and repro steps for issues.

### Phase 2 — Improve touch and layout
- Validate selection, long-press building, camera gestures, and command-card controls with actual fingers—not only automated clicks.
- Check target sizes, accidental gesture conflicts, and thumb reach in portrait.
- Verify that key information and controls remain visible around notches and browser safe areas.
- Preserve the existing tap and camera safeguards documented in `AGENTS.md`.

### Phase 3 — Optimize based on measurements
- Profile rendering in `src/presentation/renderer.js`, especially shadows, antialiasing, and per-frame texture work.
- If weaker devices struggle, add a small set of graphics-quality options or sensible device-aware defaults.
- Measure performance with many units and buildings on screen, not just at the main menu.
- Keep the fixed-step simulation and bounded catch-up behavior in `src/main.js`.

### Phase 4 — Test lifecycle and persistence
- Check behavior when the browser is backgrounded, the screen is locked, the device rotates, or the page is reloaded.
- Confirm saves and profile data recover as expected from `src/core/engine.js`.
- Decide whether the game needs an explicit pause/resume experience when the browser loses focus.

### Phase 5 — Decide how to distribute it
- Continue with the static mobile-web version if browser access is sufficient.
- Consider a PWA or app wrapper only if installation, store presence, or native platform features are important goals.

## Recommended next step

Start with **Phase 1**, then address the most visible touch or performance problem found on real devices. The project already documents several mobile-specific pitfalls in `AGENTS.md`, and its browser verification recipe is useful for layout checks; real-device testing should complement it.

1. **[P1] Manual save can report success when the save failed.**

   The page opts into edge-to-edge viewport layout and accounts for the *top* inset, but the minimap, selection card, and toolbar use fixed bottom offsets; the minimap and selection card also use fixed side offsets. On devices with a home-indicator area or landscape notches, those overlays may sit too close to system UI.

   **Validate:** Check portrait and landscape on notched iOS devices, especially with the home indicator visible, and confirm the HUD remains reachable and unobstructed.

3. **[P2] A held pinch can accidentally trigger the long-press action.**  
   Each `pointerdown` schedules a long-press timer. When a second pointer starts a pinch, the existing timer is not cleared, so holding the pinch past 550 ms can still call `game.onLongPress()`.  
   Reference: [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/presentation/input.js:10-13`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/presentation/input.js#L10)  
   **Validate:** Start a pinch on a selected peasant and hold it for longer than 550 ms; check that it does not open the build action or show the long-press prompt.

4. **[P2] Autosave is limited to the active, unpaused game loop.**  
   The autosave counter advances only inside the `!paused && !st.over` branch. There is no page-visibility or page-lifecycle save handling in the inspected source, so a paused match or a mobile browser suspending/terminating the page may leave the last stored save stale.  
   References: [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js:322-335`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js#L322), [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js:333`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js#L333)  
   **Validate:** Pause a match, make progress, then background or close the page and continue from the save. Repeat with the match running and compare the restored state.

5. **[P2, profile needed] Rendering does per-entity canvas/texture work every frame.**  
   The main loop calls `renderer.sync` every frame, and sync redraws each entity’s health-bar canvas and marks its texture for upload even when the displayed health has not changed. The renderer also enables antialiasing and soft shadows with a pixel-ratio cap of 2. This is a credible mobile GPU/CPU workload risk, though the source alone does not establish a frame-rate failure.

1: # AGENTS.md — KINGDOMS RTS (PlayGround)
2: 
3: Mobile-first chibi-3D RTS. Static site: no build step, no package.json, no test runner.
4: `index.html` + ES modules in `src/`, Three.js r160 via CDN importmap (`unpkg.com`) — **no npm install, no node_modules, no bundler**. Deployment serves the repo root as-is.
5: 
6: `Agents.md` already holds process lifecycle + SwiftShader/playwright capture rules; this file is the code-level playbook. Note: `Agents.md` and `AGENTS.md` differ only by case — they collide on macOS/Windows checkouts, so on a case-insensitive FS edit the existing `Agents.md` instead of adding this file.
7: 
8: ## Commands
9: 
10: ```bash
11: find src -name '*.js' -exec node --check {} \;   # syntax gate; run on every touched file
12: ./start.sh                                      # static server; PORT env overrides default 3000
13: PORT=3109 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"   # what start.sh runs
14: ./capture.sh                                    # OMGithub GPU/SwiftShader capture (see Agents.md)
15: ```
16: 
17: `src/**/*.js` under plain bash has `globstar` off, so it **silently skips `src/main.js`**. Use the `find` form.
18: 
19: Headless sim — the fastest way to test balance and logic (no browser, seconds not minutes):
20: 
21: ```bash
22: node --input-type=module -e "
23: const E=await import('./src/core/engine.js'),W=await import('./src/world/world.js'),
24:       S=await import('./src/sim/sim.js'),A=await import('./src/ai/ai.js');
25: const st=E.makeState({faction:'human',aiFaction:'undead',ai:'expander',fog:'on',speed:1});
26: const map=W.genMap(42);
27: S.spawnBase(st,map,0,-30,-30,'human'); S.spawnBase(st,map,1,30,30,'undead'); W.updateFog(st,map);
28: for(let i=0;i<3000;i++){S.tick(st,map,0.1); if(i%20===0)A.aiTick(st,map); if(st.over)break;}
29: console.log('over',st.over,'t',st.t.toFixed(0));"
30: ```
31: 
32: Node-importable (no DOM/three at import time): `src/core`, `src/world`, `src/sim`, `src/ai`, `src/missions`, `src/buildings/data.js`, `src/factions/factions.js`. `src/presentation/*` imports `three` — browser only.
33: 
34: Adding a root `package.json` flips the deploy path to Vite and `start.sh` will run `vite build`; don't add one casually.
35: 
36: ## Architecture (non-obvious)
37: 
38: - **Engine owns state, presentation owns pixels.** `core/engine.js` holds a plain-object `st` + entity list; `sim/sim.js:tick()` is the only mutator; `main.js:loop()` is a fixed 10 Hz accumulator (`STEP=0.1`, max 5 substeps/frame) decoupled from `requestAnimationFrame`.
39: - **Resource keys are `gold` / `wood` only.** Never write `st.res[o][kind]` with a raw kind string — `gather` carries `kind2:'gold'|'tree'` and must map `tree → wood` in the deposit branch. This exact bug shipped once.
40: - **Faction scaling** goes through `factionMult(owner)` → keys `hp/dmg/cost/speed/build/archer/wood/gold` plus signature keys `gather/produce/range/bldHp/regen/regrow/burn/raise`; missing keys must fall back (`?? 1`).
